scope: One source-locked mapping of the manuscript's fresh initial-state augmentation and seven-row reversible compiler to pinned Lean control, history and local-step definitions; distinguish the machine-level bridge from exact planar compiler/field equivalence.

findings.fresh_initial_state: Source 379 compiler section explicitly inserts q_start with unchanged symbol and head, then enters former initial state, before defining the seven-row reversible recorder. Pinned Lean FreshMachine.freshMachine adds state 0, shifts old state q to q+1, inserts a state-0 instruction some (1,a,(1 : Fin 3)), and shifts old target states. The Fin 3 movement encoding is converted to signed movement by subtracting 1 in RecorderMachine.ofMachine and FiniteRecorder.finiteMachine, so this inserted step is stationary. This is the same one-step normalization PURPOSE, not a byte-identical machine table.
findings.fresh_step_proved_in_lean: FreshMachine.lean contains freshMachine_initial_step, freshMachine_step_lift, freshInput_configuration and freshInput_halts_iff. In particular configurationAt(freshInput I)(n+1)=liftConfiguration(configurationAt I n) under ValidInput, and Halts(freshInput I) iff Halts(I). This identifies a positive input-level one-step simulation already proved for Lean's own machine. The source manuscript gives the corresponding informal construction, but no source-to-Lean definitional equality is asserted.

control_history_dictionary.source (data,mark,history): Lean Symbol=(data,history,mark); a permutation of the last two components

seven_rows.guard: nonhalting checkpoint, history != frontier, marker false

findings.compiler_table_bridge: FiniteRecorder.instructionTable enumerates finite controls and symbols, evaluates the seven-row evalLocal, and mem_instructionTable_iff identifies table membership with LocalStep. Branches.compileBranches then expands every instruction-table entry over allSymbols for the left-neighbor digit; this branch expansion is NOT the same as the source's coarse right/stay rectangle enumeration (already recorded in PR #467).
findings.recorder_and_observer: RecorderRun.checkpointAt initializes frontier at g0=2 and empty history elsewhere with false marker; checkpoint_successor and halting_checkpoint_iff establish Lean recorder simulation. FiniteRecorder.finite_recorder_halts_iff and PlanarRecorder.step_realized/run_observer_iff connect its own encoded points to affine moves and observation; PlanarInitialShift.normalized_run_observer_iff includes the fresh-state shift. These are preexisting pinned Lean statements, not a new Lean proof.
findings.exact_limit: The source says it normalizes to a single halting state and total nonhalting table; Lean normalizes instructions and uses a freshMachine and finiteMachine construction. The exact input-machine representation, source compiler's state/alphabet enumerations, source geometric state-square offsets, branch indices, and spatial field are not shown definitionally equal. A row-by-row dictionary plus one-step Lean simulation is insufficient for complete manuscript-to-Lean theorem equivalence.

replay.method: Authenticated GitHub exact-commit fetch_file, GitHub-reported Git blob SHA comparisons and literal anchor substring assertions; no shell/Lean compilation.
replay.proof_scope: Source-to-Lean syntactic/structural correspondence and identification of existing Lean theorems, not independently checked Lean kernel replay or proof validity.

next_obligation: Identify the source's normalized machine/table against Lean's freshMachine+finiteMachine on a concrete common machine input, then compare branch enumerations and digit/geometry parameters; do not infer whole-rectangle equivalence from encoded orbit equivalence.
